managementTone.evidenceNotes: Jassy provided granular capex ROI data ('clear line of sight to strong financial returns'), quantified AI ARR for first time ($25B), gave 30-year datacenter lifespan economics. Deflected FTC questions. Did not address open-source competitive threat directly.

dodgedQuestions: Specific FTC trial preparation and remedy scenarios
Whether open-source AI models are impacting cloud API demand
Exact timeline for FCF to return positive
surprisingQuestions: Anthropic valuation dependency — what happens if AI startup valuations deflate?
Whether $220B includes potential acquisitions or is purely organic infrastructure
newConcernsVsPrior: Memory cost inflation (not discussed last quarter — drove the $20B capex raise)
AI revenue disclosure ($25B ARR — first time quantified, previously only 'multi-billion')

keyQuotes.speaker: Andy Jassy
keyQuotes.quote: At this level of spend and higher, we have clear line-of-sight to strong financial returns
keyQuotes.context: Responding to capex ROI concern — the 12 words that moved the stock
keyQuotes.reliability: high — backed by $496B backlog data and specific datacenter economics

keyQuotes.speaker: Andy Jassy
keyQuotes.quote: AWS could eventually become a trillion dollar annual revenue business
keyQuotes.context: Long-term vision framing, citing 'striking' AI demand

keyQuotes.speaker: Andy Jassy
keyQuotes.quote: Data centers have useful lives of 30 years or more. Inside each facility, we can cycle through five or six generations of servers.
keyQuotes.context: Justifying the $220B spend as long-duration infrastructure, not short-cycle hardware

keyQuotes.speaker: Brian Olsavsky
keyQuotes.quote: The increase to $220B was primarily driven by higher memory costs
keyQuotes.context: Explaining mid-year capex raise — not demand increase but input cost inflation

newTopics: AI revenue ARR disclosed for first time ($25B)
Memory cost inflation as capex driver (new)
droppedTopics: International profitability concerns (no longer questioned — margins stable)
sentimentDelta.note: This was the strongest management confidence performance in at least 4 quarters. The shift from 'we're spending for the future' to 'we have clear line of sight to returns' was the key narrative pivot.

scores.summary: Management convincingly addressed capex ROI (the #1 concern) with specific economics, but left FCF timeline vague and dodged FTC/competitive questions entirely. The market scored it a pass — +15% after hours.
